messages:
maria: Heads up — we're getting a spike of 429s for org:acme even though the usage dashboard shows ~60% of quota. Not a full outage but steady rejects from the enforcer since ~08:12 UTC. Anyone else seeing this?

sam: saw alerts. Quick sanity: are these per-key or per-org rejections?

maria: per-org. Keys look fine. Example rejection: 
```
{"reason":"quota_exceeded","org":"acme","window_start":1789993600,"window_end":1789997200,"count":1200}
```

jess: pulling enforcement logs now. Initial read — enforcer is using aggregator_snapshot_ts=1789993500 for some buckets while ingest shows last_event_ts ~1789997000. That smells like collector<->aggregator clock skew or delayed commits.

ron: yesterday we rotated the aggregator consumers to a new kafka group id during the deploy window, could that explain it?

sam: possibly. If the aggregator was restarted and had to reprocess, the snapshot used by enforcer might lag behind live events. Enforcer reads the latest committed snapshot from Dynamo (aggregator writes). If writer was paused, snapshot ts will be stale.

jess: quick checks: kafka consumer lag for topic usage-events: partitions 0..11 show 0-2k lag but partition 7 has 45k. That's the org:acme partition.

maria: aha. Partitioning by org hash means heavy customers can concentrate on a single partition. Did the consumer rebalance happen?

ron: yes — we had a rebalance. consumer group consumer-usage-agg got rebalanced -> one pod got stuck in CrashLoop for ~3m, backlog built up.

sam: fixes: 1) drain consumer, 2) bump consumer parallelism for heavy partitions, 3) have enforcer fallback to recent streaming counters if snapshot ts < now - 5m. Which is the least risky short-term?

jess: short-term: backfill the aggregator snapshot for affected orgs and increase burst for that org to avoid immediate rejects while backfill catches up. Backfill script exists: 
```
# backfill usage for org
python tools/backfill_org_usage.py --org acme --from-ts 1789993000 --to-ts 1789998000
```

maria: can we do automated fallback in enforcer without a deploy? Maybe a feature flag toggle?

sam: the code already has a flag but it's server-side config pushed via config-service. We can flip it in config-service without a code deploy. The flag is enforcer.use_streaming_if_snapshot_stale=true.

ron: I'll flip the flag for the org with a targeted config override for 1h. Then run the backfill.

jess: flipping now. deploy-bot: note the change?

deploy-bot: config-service: enforcer.use_streaming_if_snapshot_stale=true for overrides/orgs/acme set by ron at 2026-03-18T08:40:12Z :white_check_mark:

maria: after flip, we've seen rejects drop by 90% within 30s. Dashboard still shows snapshot_ts lag but streaming counters are applied. Good quick mitigation.

sam: longer term we need: 1) smarter partitioning (avoid hot-partition collisions), 2) better consumer autoscaling / probe to avoid stuck pods, 3) reconciliation job that compares snapshot_ts vs last_event_ts and auto-backfills or raises early warnings.

jess: also add enforcer telemetry: expose snapshot_age metric per-org + reason code when enforcement uses snapshot vs streaming so SLOs can track.

maria: filed infra ticket and linked notes: https://redwood.svc/ops/infra/INC-4821 — includes root cause, mitigation (config flip + backfill), and next actions.

ron: running backfill now — ETA ~7m. Progress logs: 
```
[08:46:01] backfill start for org acme
[08:48:12] processed 120k events, remaining 15k
[08:52:30] completed, wrote snapshot ts=1789998000
```

maria: confirm enforcer now reads snapshot_ts==1789998000 and rejects are gone.

sam: can we add a safe-mode in enforcer: if snapshot_age > threshold and streaming rate > threshold, auto-apply a temporary burst allowance of +20% for 5m? Make it toggleable.

jess: agree. Also let's add alerting for partition lag > 10k for >2m with an annotated runbook that suggests increasing consumer parallelism or triggering targeted backfill.

maria: I'll draft UX for console: show 'quota health' panel with snapshot_age, streaming_rate, partition_lag, and quick actions (increase burst, trigger backfill, view event log). That should help CS too.

ron: after-action checklist we agreed on in thread: 
- add snapshot_age metric + dashboard
- add enforcer fallback flag + enable by default for the auto-override path behind a kill switch
- improve partition distribution for top 1% orgs
- add runbook for consumer rebalance/backfill
- instrument rejected events with which source (snapshot vs streaming) caused enforcement

maria: great. I'll open follow-ups and assign. Thanks team :handshake: Everyone who helped — please add any missed items here.

sam: add a regression test in CI that simulates consumer pause + spike to validate enforcer fallback path.

jess: and add k8s liveness probe adjustment for consumer pods to avoid long stuck states.

ron: closing thread once tickets are in. I'll post postmortem summary in #incidents later.

maria: ok closing — we can re-open if anything pops up. :sparkles:
